steps.label: TorchInductor
steps.sub: compiles fused, optimized kernels from it

code:
model = MyModel().to("cuda")
compiled_model = torch.compile(model)

for x, y in train_loader:
    out = compiled_model(x)
    loss = loss_fn(out, y)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    optimizer.zero_grad()
caption: The training loop itself doesn't change at all.

eyebrow: First call: slow. Every call after: fast.
code:
t0 = time.time()
compiled_model(inputs)   # traces + compiles
print(time.time() - t0)  # seconds

t0 = time.time()
compiled_model(inputs)   # reuses compiled graph
print(time.time() - t0)  # milliseconds
caption: Only worth it once you have enough iterations to amortize that cost.
